questions.question: Select the idiom that can correctly replace the underlined part of the given sentence. I know she really wants the promotion, but she really hit me below the hand by telling the boss about my personal problems.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the idiom that can correctly replace the underlined part of the given sentence.

I know she really wants the promotion, but she really hit me below the hand by telling the boss about my personal problems.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4), i.e., 'hit me below the belt.'

Key Points

  • The error lies in Part (hit me below the hand) of the sentence.
  • As per instructions, the remaining portion of the sentence is correct.
  • In the given sentence the idiom 'hit me below the hand' is incorrect.
  • Here we need to use the correct idiom 'hit me below the belt', which means to say something that is often too personal, usually irrelevant, and always unfair. (ऐसा कुछ कहना जो अक्सर बहुत व्यक्तिगत होता है, आमतौर पर अप्रासंगिक और हमेशा अनुचित होता है)
  • Example:
    • Mike was upset recently by being hit below the belt.
  • Therefore, in the erroneous part, the use of 'hit me below the hand' in the sentence should be replaced with 'hit me below the belt' to make it grammatically correct.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 

Correct sentence: I know she really wants the promotion, but she really hit me below the belt by telling the boss about my personal problems.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. From scratch
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

From scratch
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2.

Key Points

  • The idiom "From scratch" means starting from the very beginning without any prior preparation or advantage. (शुरुआत से)
    • Example: After losing all his savings, he had to start his business from scratch.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • From a skin disease (त्वचा की बीमारी से): This option is incorrect as it is unrelated to the idiom.
    • Example: He suffered from a skin disease that required immediate medical attention.
  • From utter disorder (पूर्ण अव्यवस्था से): This option is incorrect as it does not convey the meaning of starting afresh.
    • Example: The room was in utter disorder after the party.
  • From death (मृत्यु से): This option is incorrect as it is not related to the idiom.
    • Example: The doctor saved him from death with timely intervention.

questions.question: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the given idiom. By fair means or foul
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the given idiom.

By fair means or foul

Key Points

  • The idiom "By fair means or foul" means achieving something by any possible method, whether it is honest or dishonest. (ईमानदारी या बेईमानी से किसी चीज को प्राप्त करना)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The judge wanted to hear straight from the horse’s mouth .
questions.questionHtml:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Directly from the person involved.

Key Points

  • The idiom "straight from the horse's mouth" means getting information directly from the person who has direct knowledge or experience of it. (सीधे स्रोत से प्राप्त जानकारी)
    • Example: If you want to know about the new project, ask John. He got the details straight from the horse's mouth.
  • "Directly from the person involved" means obtaining information from the person who is directly connected with the matter. (प्रत्यक्ष रूप से शामिल व्यक्ति से जानकारी प्राप्त करना)
    • Example: The CEO's resignation was confirmed directly from the person involved during the press conference.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Directly from the lawyer (प्रत्यक्ष रूप से वकील से): Receiving information from the lawyer.
    • Example: The details of the case were provided directly from the lawyer during the hearing.
  • In close vicinity to the juror (जूरी सदस्य के निकट): Being near to the juror.
    • Example: The witness was seated in close vicinity to the juror to ensure clear communication.
  • Having ears which never fail (ऐसे कान जो कभी असफल नहीं होते): Having perfect hearing ability.
    • Example: Grandma has ears which never fail; she can hear even the faintest sounds.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Be like chalk and cheese
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Be like chalk and cheese

options.text: To be completely different from each other
options.html: To be completely different from each other

options.text: To be very similar to each other
options.html: To be very similar to each other

options.text: To have a close relation with another person
options.html: To have a close relation with another person

options.text: To be distantly related to each other
options.html: To be distantly related to each other

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: To be completely different from each other.

Key Points

  • The idiom "Be like chalk and cheese" means two things or people that are completely different from each other. (एकदम अलग)
    • Example: Despite being twins, John and Jake are like chalk and cheese in their personalities.
  • "To be completely different from each other" refers to having no similarities at all, often in terms of characteristics, preferences, or nature. (पूरी तरह से अलग होना)
    • Example: Her approach to solving problems is completely different from mine; we are like chalk and cheese.
  • Hence, the idiom "Be like chalk and cheese" means to be completely different from each other.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To be completely different from each other.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • To be very similar to each other (एक दूसरे के बहुत समान होना): Sharing many of the same characteristics or qualities.
    • Example: The two sisters are very similar to each other in appearance and mannerisms.
  • To have a close relation with another person (किसी अन्य व्यक्ति के साथ निकट संबंध होना): Being emotionally or socially close to someone.
    • Example: She has a very close relation with her best friend from childhood.
  • To be distantly related to each other (एक दूसरे से दूर का संबंध होना): Having a distant familial or social connection.
    • Example: They are distantly related to each other through a common ancestor.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A storm in a teacup
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A storm in a teacup
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Much excitement over something trivial.

Key Points

  • The idiom "A storm in a teacup" means a lot of unnecessary anger and worry about a matter that is not important. (छोटी सी बात पर ज्यादा हंगामा करना)
    • Example: Everyone is upset about the minor issue, but it’s just a storm in a teacup.
  • "Much excitement over something trivial" refers to making a big deal out of something insignificant. (तुच्छ बात पर अधिक उत्साह)
    • Example: They argued over who should wash the dishes, but it’s just much excitement over something trivial.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Much excitement over something trivial.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • A signal for upcoming storm (आने वाले तूफान का संकेत): An indication that a storm is going to occur.
    • Example: The dark clouds in the sky are a signal for an upcoming storm.
  • Easy money (आसान पैसा): Money that is earned with little or no effort.
    • Example: He thought investing in stocks would be easy money, but he lost everything.
  • Suffering in silence (चुपचाप पीड़ित होना): Enduring pain or hardship without complaining or showing it.
    • Example: Despite his illness, he continued working, suffering in silence.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The shopkeeper was sly as a fox and tried to sell off the old stock.

Key Points

  • The idiom "sly as a fox" means someone who is very clever, cunning, and able to deceive others for personal gain. (बहुत चालाक)
    • Example: The negotiator was sly as a fox, always securing the best deals for his clients.
  • "smart and clever" refers to someone who is intelligent and able to think quickly or understand things easily. (चतुर और समझदार)
    • Example: She is smart and clever, always coming up with innovative solutions to problems.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. smart and clever.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Slow (धीमा): Lacking speed or quickness in movement or action.
    • Example: The old man was slow in his movements, taking his time to cross the street.
  • Suspicious (संदिग्ध): Having or showing a cautious distrust of someone or something.
    • Example: The detective was suspicious of the man's alibi.
  • In confusion or disagreement (उलझन या असहमति में): Being in a state of not understanding or not being in agreement.
    • Example: The team was in confusion or disagreement about the best strategy to adopt.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Day and night
questions.questionHtml:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Continuously.

Key Points

  • The idiom "day and night" means something that happens continuously without stopping. (दिन-रात)
    • Example: She worked day and night to finish the project on time.
  • "Continuously" refers to something that occurs without interruption or pause. (लगातार)
    • Example: The machine operates continuously for 24 hours.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Continuously. 

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Clumsily (अनाड़ीपन से): In a way that lacks skill or finesse.
    • Example: He handled the delicate vase clumsily and nearly dropped it.
  • Adversely (प्रतिकूल रूप से): In a way that prevents success or development; harmfully.
    • Example: The new policy will adversely affect small businesses.
  • Diligently (परिश्रमपूर्वक): In a way that shows care and conscientiousness in one's work or duties.
    • Example: She diligently completed all her assignments on time.

questions.solution:

Key Points

  • The idiom "on thin ice" means to be in a situation that is risky or precarious, where there is danger of some bad consequence. (संकटपूर्ण स्थिति में)
    • Example: After the scandal, the politician was on thin ice with his party.
  • "In a precarious or risky situation" refers to a state where there is a high chance of danger or failure; it implies uncertainty and instability. (जोखिमपूर्ण स्थिति में)
    • Example: Investing all your money in one venture is like putting yourself in a precarious or risky situation.
  • Hence, we can infer that the most appropriate meaning of the idiom "on thin ice" is to be "In a precarious or risky situation".

Therefore, the correct answer is: In a precarious or risky situation.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • In a situation of comfort (आराम की स्थिति में): Being in a state where there is no worry or discomfort.
    • Example: After years of hard work, he is now in a situation of comfort, without any financial worries.
  • Forcing itself to collaborate (सहयोग के लिए मजबूर): Being compelled to work together with others, possibly against one's own desires.
    • Example: The two rival companies were forcing themselves to collaborate for the greater good of the industry.
  • Depending on business competitors (व्यापारिक प्रतियोगियों पर निर्भर): Relying on the actions or decisions of competitors in the business environment.
    • Example: The small start-up was depending on business competitors to set the market prices.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Cup of tea
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Cup of tea
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Something one likes/excels in.

Key Points

  • The idiom "Cup of tea" is often used in English to describe something that one finds particularly enjoyable or that one is particularly good at. It is not related to the literal act of drinking tea but is a metaphorical expression. (पसंद)
    • Example: Rock climbing really isn't my cup of tea; I prefer hiking.
  • The phrase "Something one likes/excels in" perfectly encapsulates the essence of the idiom 'Cup of tea', indicating a preference or an area of expertise. (पसंद करना/में उत्कृष्ट होना)
    • Example: Puzzle games are really my cup of tea; I love the challenge they present.
  • Thus, the idiom 'Cup of tea' is best explained by Option 4, which signifies personal preference or skill.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Something one likes/excels in.
